data.name: Prove the quadrilateral total

data.name: Explain the mathematics

data.name: Explain the rule
data.narration: A regular polygon has exterior angle three hundred and sixty divided by its number of sides. The interior-angle sum is sides minus two, multiplied by one hundred and eighty.

data.name: Prove the interior angle
data.narration: An interior angle is one hundred and eighty minus the exterior angle. That works for every regular polygon.

data.name: Regular polygons
data.narration: Regular means all sides equal and all angles equal. The equilateral triangle and the square are regular too. A hexagon has three pairs of parallel sides.
data.prompt: What makes a polygon regular?

data.name: One property: right angle
data.narration: Sorting asks one question of every shape: does it have this property? A right angle is a square corner. Rectangles, squares and one triangle have them.
data.prompt: How many shapes have a right angle?

data.name: Name the shape
data.narration: Opposite sides parallel and equal, but no right angles: this is a parallelogram. Its area is base times height: 4 times 3, which is 12.
data.prompt: What is this shape called?

data.name: Work backwards
data.narration: A square has perimeter 36 centimetres and four equal sides. Share it out: 36 divided by 4 is 9, so each side is 9 centimetres.
data.prompt: What is 36 divided by 4?

data.name: Why 25 works
data.narration: Fit four copies of the triangle inside a 7 by 7 square. The big square is 49, the four triangles use 4 times 6, which is 24, so the tilted square is 49 minus 24, which is 25.
data.prompt: What is 49 minus 24?

data.name: The slanted side is a trap
data.narration: The slanted side is 5 long, but it is not the height. 6 times 5 gives 30, which is too big. Use the straight-up height: 6 times 4 is 24.
data.prompt: Why is 6 × 5 wrong?

data.name: The height can sit outside
data.narration: In an obtuse triangle the top corner leans past the base. Extend the base with a dotted line and measure straight up to it. The rule still works: half times 4 times 4 is 8.
data.prompt: Why extend the base?

data.name: Right-angled trapezium
data.narration: The rule works for any trapezium, even one with a vertical side. Parallel sides 3 and 7, height 4: half times 10 times 4 is 20.
data.prompt: Which side is the height here?

data.name: Not side times side
data.narration: The rhombus has sides of 5. Squaring the side gives 25, which is not the area. Use the diagonals: 24.
data.prompt: Why is 5 × 5 wrong?

data.name: Perimeter with a curve
data.narration: Walk round the outside: bottom 8, two sides of 4, and the curved edge. The arc is half a circumference, pi times 4, about 12.57. Total about 28.57.
data.prompt: Is the straight edge across the top part of the perimeter?

data.name: The label of a can
data.narration: Peel the label off a can and lay it flat: a rectangle as long as the circumference. Its area is circumference times height, which gives the curved surface area.
data.prompt: What shape is the unrolled label?

data.name: Area or circumference?
data.narration: Do not mix them up. Area is π times radius squared, 78.5, in square units. Circumference is 2 times π times radius, 31.4, in plain units. Square the radius, do not double it.
data.prompt: Which one uses r squared?

data.name: Big sectors
data.narration: The method works above 180 degrees too. 270 degrees is three quarters of the circle: arc 28.27, area 84.82.
data.prompt: What fraction is 270 degrees?

data.name: Longer round, not bigger
data.narration: Do not assume a longer perimeter means a bigger area. A is 10 by 1: perimeter 22, area only 10. B is 5 by 5: perimeter 20, area 25.
data.prompt: Which has the bigger area, A or B?

data.name: Square kilometres
data.narration: A kilometre is 1000 metres, so a square kilometre is 1000 times 1000, which is 1 000 000 square metres. One block here is 100 m by 100 m, 10 000 square metres, and there are 100 blocks.
data.prompt: How many square metres in a square kilometre?

data.name: Check your counting
data.narration: This pyramid has a square base and four triangular sides. It has five faces, eight edges and five vertices. Now explore the other solids.
data.prompt: Does the point at the top count as a vertex?

data.name: Build a pyramid
data.narration: Four triangles fold towards a single point above the square base, making a pyramid.
data.prompt: Why does this solid have five faces?

data.name: Count the hidden cubes
data.narration: Some cubes are behind or beneath other cubes. Remember their full columns before you count the total.
data.prompt: What is the total number of cubes?

data.name: Hidden cubes need more thinking
data.narration: Some cubes can hide behind others. You cannot always reconstruct every hidden cube from plans and elevations alone. Use all three views and make a model that fits each one.
data.prompt: Could two different solids have the same three views?

data.name: Volume is space, not surface
data.narration: Count the solid unit cubes, including hidden cubes inside the stack. Volume measures the space filled, not the number of visible faces or surface squares.
data.prompt: What should you count when a cube is hidden?

data.name: The universal rule
data.narration: Every prism follows the same rule: volume equals cross-sectional area multiplied by perpendicular length.
data.prompt: Which measurement must you calculate first?

data.name: Transfer to another cuboid
data.narration: The same formulas work when the dimensions change. Here the volume is thirty cubic units and the surface area is sixty-two square units.
data.prompt: Which calculation gives the surface area of this new cuboid?

data.name: Transfer to a tall cylinder
data.narration: For radius one and height five, curved area is ten pi and both ends total two pi.
data.prompt: Find the new total surface area in terms of pi.

data.name: Use the general rule
data.narration: This works whenever the two solids have equal base areas and equal perpendicular heights. A pyramid or cone takes one third.
data.prompt: What stays the same when we change the dimensions?

data.name: A sphere of radius two
data.narration: Change the radius to two. Surface area becomes sixteen pi square units, while volume is thirty-two pi over three cubic units.
data.prompt: What stays the same about the formulas when the radius changes?

data.name: Move off centre
data.narration: Move away from the centre and the sphere section gets smaller. At a distance of one point eight units, its section area is five point seven six pi square units.
data.prompt: Can a sphere section shrink while the sphere stays unchanged?

data.name: Convert with confidence
data.narration: Remember: one cubic centimetre equals one millilitre, one thousand cubic centimetres equal one litre, and one cubic metre equals one thousand litres.
data.prompt: Which conversion will help you in a question about water?

data.name: Add all four triangles
data.narration: The base covers sixteen squares. Each triangle covers six. Four triangles add twenty-four, so total area is forty square units.
data.prompt: Why is the answer forty square units?

data.name: One, square, cube
data.narration: Remember these three linked rules. Length times k. Surface area times k squared. Volume times k cubed. One and a half cubed is three point three seven five.
data.prompt: Which power of k belongs to the amount of space inside?

data.name: Apply the law

STEPS.text: An inside number has two parents. One plus one makes two.
STEPS.prompt: Trace the two numbers above the two.

STEPS.name: build-the-fourth-row
STEPS.text: To make three, add the one and two directly above it. Repeat across the row.
STEPS.prompt: Can you explain why both middle entries are three?

STEPS.name: build-five-rows
STEPS.text: Three plus three gives six. The new row is one, four, six, four, one.
STEPS.prompt: Find the two parent numbers that make six.

STEPS.name: row-sums-double
STEPS.text: The row totals are one, two, four, eight, sixteen and thirty-two. Each total doubles.
STEPS.prompt: Predict the total of the next row.

STEPS.name: triangles-hidden-in-a-triangle
STEPS.text: Look diagonally. One, three, six, ten, fifteen are triangular numbers hidden inside Pascal’s triangle.
STEPS.prompt: Explain why that diagonal grows by one more each step.

data.name: multiplying-instead
data.narration: Two, four, eight, sixteen. The amounts added change, but doubling works every time.
data.prompt: Why is add two not the rule for the whole sequence?

data.name: continue-a-double
data.narration: Doubling is different from adding. Two, four, eight, sixteen, thirty-two.
data.prompt: Explain why a fixed addition cannot generate every term.

data.name: koch-repeat-length
data.narration: Each of the four sections becomes four more. Four times four makes sixteen sections.
data.prompt: If the first line was nine centimetres, explain why iteration two totals sixteen centimetres.
